idea: Asia investor roadshow organisation for European small caps
buyer: IR teams at European small and mid caps
pain: They want Asian investors but have no route to them
channel: Asia contacts plus corporate access networks
verdict: A real service with real fees, but corporate buyers are cold and brokers own this today.

why.distribution: Corporate IR teams are a cold segment for her, and Asian investor relationships need building.
why.demand: Corporate access is a paid service, currently supplied by brokers as part of bundled relationships.
why.fmf: She knows what investors want from a meeting; event logistics is not her skill.
why.defensibility: Brokers provide this free as part of the relationship.
why.leverage: Logistics-heavy work that does not scale.
why.tailwind: Flat; Asian appetite for European small caps is not growing.
why.ceiling: £20k x 10 roadshows = £200k, competing against brokers who give it away.

ceiling_arithmetic: £20k x 10 roadshows = £200k gross less ~25% travel and logistics = £150k. Ten roadshows a year is heavy logistics work, and brokers bundle this free. Realistic: 2-3 = £30-45k.
carries: Real fees and a service companies genuinely want.
kills: Brokers already provide corporate access free as a relationship service.
test: Ask two IR directors what they pay for Asian corporate access.
test_pass: They pay someone and are dissatisfied.
test_fail: Their broker arranges it at no cost.
